name: Aloo Gobi
base_instructions: Heat vegetable oil in a heavy-bottom pan and temper with cumin seeds until fragrant.
Add finely minced ginger and green chilies, sautéing for 1 minute.
Add diced potatoes and cauliflower florets; toss on medium-high heat for 4-5 minutes until lightly golden.
Stir in chopped tomatoes, turmeric powder, coriander powder, and salt.
Cover with a lid and simmer on low heat for 15-18 minutes until vegetables are fork-tender.
Sprinkle garam masala and chopped cilantro before serving hot with chapati or rice.

name: Baingan Bharta
base_instructions: Roast the whole brinjal directly over an open flame until charred and tender inside, then peel and mash.
Heat oil in a pan, add cumin seeds, chopped garlic, ginger, and diced onions; sauté until golden brown.
Add chopped tomatoes, turmeric powder, chili powder, and salt; cook until tomatoes turn soft and oil releases.
Add the mashed roasted brinjal and mix thoroughly to combine flavors.
Cook on medium-low flame for 7-8 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Garnish with fresh coriander leaves and serve warm with phulkas.

name: Tomato Rasam
base_instructions: In a pot, bring chopped tomatoes, tamarind water, rasam powder, turmeric, and salt to a rolling boil.
Simmer for 8-10 minutes until raw tamarind aroma dissipates.
Add 1.5 cups of water and bring to a gentle frothy boil, then turn off heat.
In a small tempering pan, heat ghee and crackle mustard seeds, curry leaves, and a pinch of asafoetida.
Pour the hot tempering over the rasam and garnish generously with chopped cilantro.

name: Cabbage Poriyal
base_instructions: Heat coconut oil in a pan; add mustard seeds and urad dal, letting them turn golden brown.
Add curry leaves and slit green chilies.
Add shredded cabbage, carrots, a pinch of turmeric, and salt. Toss well.
Cover and cook on low heat for 8-10 minutes without adding water until vegetables are tender yet crisp.
Stir in freshly grated coconut, mix gently, and turn off heat.

name: Mixed Vegetable Curry
base_instructions: Heat oil in a kadai and add cumin seeds until they splutter.
Add chopped onions and sauté until translucent, followed by ginger-garlic paste.
Stir in tomato puree and spices; cook until the masala leaves oil at the edges.
Add potatoes, carrots, beans, and cauliflower with 1 cup of warm water.
Cover and simmer for 12-15 minutes until vegetables are mostly cooked.
Add capsicum cubes and simmer for an additional 4 minutes to keep peppers crisp.
Finish with a spoonful of fresh cream and garam masala before serving.

name: Karela Masala
base_instructions: Toss sliced bitter gourd with 1/2 tsp salt and rest for 15 minutes, then squeeze out excess bitter water.
Heat mustard oil in a pan until lightly smoking, then reduce flame and add fennel seeds.
Add sliced onions and sauté until soft and lightly browned.
Add the bitter gourd slices and fry on medium heat for 10-12 minutes until crispy and golden.
Add chopped tomatoes, turmeric, coriander powder, amchur powder, and salt.
Cover and cook on low heat for 8 minutes until flavors meld completely.

name: Lauki Chana Dal
base_instructions: Rinse and soak chana dal for 30 minutes in warm water.
In a pressure cooker or deep pot, heat ghee and add cumin seeds and minced ginger.
Add chopped tomatoes, turmeric powder, and salt; sauté for 3 minutes until tomatoes soften.
Add soaked chana dal, cubed bottle gourd, and 2 cups of water.
Pressure cook for 4-5 whistles (or simmer covered for 25 minutes) until dal is tender but holds its shape.
Gently mash a few pieces of dal to thicken the curry, sprinkle garam masala, and serve hot.
